note: Accuracy retro mined 12 verdicts-later-corrected incidents from the gala lanes, flash50 receipts, LEDGER errata rows, OLM folds and burn_wave receipts, each with a byte-verified verbatim quote, lane of origin, named defect class, the falsifier that would have fired earlier, and a mechanism upgrade (who runs what, when); the ask's five seeded incidents all mapped (quantizer-fallout killed by ball3, OLM 18-fold vs 32-fold, selffeed-cua = arch-03 D2 corrected by stealth-tools, f-25 citation defects, w4-20 = byte-identical duplicate landing + its stale seed-seal verdict in CURRENT.md), and 'w4-20 placeholder' as a distinct verdict-correction incident was NOT found in any surface searched (flash50, queue, work, ledger, CONVO, git history) - stated as not found, not manufactured; finish-line check 34/34 quote spans byte-match, exit 0; no mag/ or tools/ code touched so the ratchet step does not fire.

rows.claim: UF-124/125/126 rows were ruled LANDED on transport success alone; their citations were placeholders (openreview id=XYZ, arxiv 2407.12345) and one misattribution, so B2-16's sweep corrected all three to STILL-OWED eight days later.
rows.quote: UF-124, UF-125, UF-126 rows landed but their answers are fabricated (placeholder and misattributed citations), so those three gaps are STILL-OWED, not closed.
rows.steal: The ledger append path runs a citation resolver before accepting verdict=LANDED on any row carrying an external URL/id: resolves to fetched bytes in-session or lands as UNVERIFIED, never LANDED; owner is the landing script, every append.
rows.falsifier: A LANDED row whose every external citation resolves to fetched bytes without a resolver pass would kill the gate's necessity (meaning lanes self-verify reliably).

rows.claim: The quantizer-fallout dispatch claimed 9 downstream tests encoded stale pack shapes with no suite receipt behind it; ball3 byte-verified all nine already healed in-commit (93f85e0dd) and the real 2 failures belonged to sibling lanes.
rows.quote: all nine named tests were already healed by the quantizer-hygiene lane's own commit 93f85e0dd
rows.steal: The orchestrator greps the suite receipt for failing node IDs and pins them into the ask before dispatching any fallout-fix lane; the receiving lane refuses an ask claiming failing tests without pinned IDs; one seat, one sitting.
rows.falsifier: A fallout lane that finds all nine green AND a cited 42:05 receipt showing those node IDs red would kill this law (tree regressed between snapshot and lane).

rows.claim: The OLM 18-lane/23-find fold was stale by the 32-return fold the next pass, and because the four fold outputs were untracked and overwritten in place, the predecessor text is unrecoverable; only headline counts survive in the supersession note.
rows.quote: folded an 18-lane / 23-find / 9-card confirmation state; the current fold holds the 32-return
rows.steal: Every fold pass writes a versioned path (DIGEST-<pass>.md) or commits the predecessor before overwrite, and the close step's byte walk records predecessor and successor headline sets with moment stamps; owner is the fold lane, every pass.
rows.falsifier: A consumer differencing the 18-fold against the 32-fold without naming moments and finding a real regression (not a phantom) would kill the moment-verdict framing.

rows.claim: arch-03 ruled 'selffeed is dead in situ: 9/9 ERR'; the wave5-repair stealth-tools lane re-diagnosed the rc=1 as a misresolved seat python riding a wedged cua-driver pipe and proved selffeed alive with a real m7 output in 42s.
rows.quote: selffeed rc=1 was a misresolved seat python riding a wedged cua-driver pipe
rows.steal: Any instrument lane writing a dead/broken verdict first re-runs the target once through the probe's own invocation path with a resolved interpreter and names that check in the receipt before the LEDGER row; owner is the instrument lane author, at receipt write time.
rows.falsifier: A probe-observed failure whose cause is confirmed inside the target despite the resolved-interpreter re-run would kill the separation rule.

rows.claim: f-25's playbook audit found 3 citation defects in the operating playbook (law 4 imprecise predicate, law 6 wrong path core/src/compact/policy.ts not runtime/compact/, law 8 uncited, cap 30,000 bytes not 30 KiB), and the corrections were never folded back: the wrong path is still at HEAD line 29.
rows.steal: A citation linter runs at filing time: every file:line citation in a doctrine/receipt must resolve (path exists, line range non-empty, token overlap) or the claim downgrades before landing; owner is the filing lane, wired into the pre-push hook like the ratchet.
rows.falsifier: A sweep of all doctrine citations finding zero wrong paths, empty ranges, or missing citations would kill the linter's necessity.

rows.claim: The 1,341 tests headline was hand-copied into durable docs and never byte-backed; the 09-14 trio it mis-summarized actually sums to 1,348, and the wrong number rode 12 days until B2-215's tripwire and B2-214's re-landed census.
rows.quote: "34 failed / 1305 passed / 9 skipped" sums to 1,348, not 1,341.
rows.steal: A count entering a durable doc is re-run from the named instrument at write time and carries date+instrument next to the claim; census_drift_patrol.py (--collect deep check) is the standing enforcement, MagCensusPatrolDaily 08:30.
rows.falsifier: A hand-copied count that still matches a fresh instrument re-run months later would kill the law's practical necessity (copies staying true).

rows.claim: Four self-feed numbering erratum rows in one 2026-09-26 window (B2-374, B2-383, B2-94, B2-96): concurrent board writes invalidated each lane's tail read between read and append, so the claimed brief numbers were false and stood corrected only by erratum (e.g. 441-443 became 444-446).
rows.quote: they stand as B2-444, B2-445, B2-446 per the B2-167 highest+1 renumber law
rows.steal: The queue landing close step re-reads board-highest AFTER its append and auto-emits the correction row in the B2-167 shape when appended numbers mismatch post-append truth; owner is the close step of every self-feeding lane, every close.
rows.falsifier: A window with concurrent self-feeds and zero numbering errata with no post-append re-read in the code would kill the law (read-then-write is safe under real concurrency).

rows.claim: The B2-53 queue repair's startswith prefix filter deleted six pre-existing concurrent-lane lines; four were restored verbatim from the owning lanes' scripts and two are unrecoverable from any on-disk source - a correction that destroyed evidence instead of misstating it.
rows.quote: a startswith prefix filter deleted six pre-existing concurrent-lane lines claiming B2-125/126/127
rows.steal: Any script rewriting QUEUE.md/LEDGER.jsonl (rather than appending) counts lines before and after and refuses to commit any negative delta its own diff does not name; owner is the repair script author, in the same process, every run.
rows.falsifier: A whole-file rewrite with a legitimately smaller line count whose every removed line is named in the script's own diff would show the refusal firing correctly - the law is killed only if refusals block legitimate named rewrites.

rows.claim: afterparty t30's dispatch premise 'souls table type any' was false (line 16 was already typed at HEAD) and the real TypeError was the gate's repo-root analyze phantom; the same lane found the gate's display cap over dual-path duplicated output was hiding five real findings.
rows.quote: the item premise 'souls table type any' is false
rows.steal: Defect-fix asks carry the named line's current bytes or the receiving lane reads them first and files a premise correction; every capped display reports unique-findings vs shown-count (t30's dedupe pass + count line + cap 20 to 40 is the landed standard).
rows.falsifier: A defect-fix ask whose named-line premise was true at HEAD and needed no correction would show the read-first gate firing without waste (the law is about the gate existing, not about every premise being false).

rows.claim: flash50/w4-20.md and flash50/w4-singularity.md are byte-identical duplicates (sha256 f873a43aaf1d241f, 18,212 bytes, both committed in 1ba61713d) while the wave5-repair QC validated only the w4-20 path: one receipt, two truth paths, citation graphs forked.
rows.quote: w4-20.md sha256=f873a43aaf1d241f bytes=18212; w4-singularity.md sha256=f873a43aaf1d241f bytes=18212; identical=True
rows.steal: The next bank-walking census/QC lane computes sha256 across the receipt bank and flags byte-identical pairs before the next drift-patrol commit; one path becomes canonical, the other a stub pointer naming it.
rows.falsifier: A byte-identical pair where both paths are deliberately maintained as mirrors with a documented sync check would kill the flag's necessity (duplicates would be governed, not accidental).

rows.claim: state/CURRENT.md's seed-seal section recorded the 09-26 drift member TRUST_BYTES_LAW.md; w4-20's live verify_seal.py re-run (exit 1, 56/57) found the drift had moved to engines/key_law.py, so the doc's verdict named a break that no longer existed.
rows.quote: So the drift has MOVED since the 09-26 record
rows.steal: The seal verify runs on a schedule (census_patrol-style task, one sitting to register) and the CURRENT.md seed-seal section is refreshed from the run's own output or carries the run's timestamp and result next to the claim; a doc describing a state it did not measure today carries the measurement date.
rows.falsifier: A recorded drift-member verdict still matching a fresh verify_seal.py months later would kill the decay law (the state is stable enough that records do not rot).

rows.claim: UF-128 landed with a false tool claim ('ripgrep follows symlinks by default') riding otherwise-sound delivery; the sweep's fact-check killed it because rg skips symlinks unless --follow.
rows.steal: Folded into the citation-resolution gate: tool-behavior claims in landed answers carry a one-line repro command run at filing; owner is the filing lane, every landed answer containing a tool-behavior claim.
rows.falsifier: A landed tool-behavior claim proven wrong despite a repro command having been run at filing would kill the gate (the repro itself was insufficient).
